Aerial Wildlife Survey Report  
Sheep Management Areas 7 and 8 Bighorn sheep Survey (2018-19) 
Background 
Sheep Management Areas 7 and 8 are made up of the mountainous habitats located, respectively, between 
Highway 16 and Sheep Creek (WMUs 439, 440, 441, 444, and the southern portion of 442) and from Sheep Creek 
north to the Wapiti River and west to the British Columbia border (WMUs 445, 446 and the northern portion of 
442).  
Trophy sheep hunting in these units is a general season from August 25 to October 31, for 4/5 curl rams, with the 
exception of WMU 446 and WMU 444 north of the Beaverdam road, where trophy sheep hunting is managed by 
special licenses with the same size and season restrictions. Hunting of ewes and lambs is also by special license 
in all these WMUs, from Sept 10 to October 31, with generally low realized harvest rates (example 1 to 3% of the 
previous winter’s total count). 
Funding for these surveys was provided by the Wild Sheep Foundation.  
Survey Method 
A Bell 206 helicopter was flown counter-clockwise around the mountain ridges of each distinct winter range, at an 
elevation between the ridgetop and tree line.  Sheep were classified from the helicopter, and were also 
photographed using a Nikon D3200 with an 18-140 mm lens to verify the field classification.   
 
A total of 46.2 hours were flown on:  
 
 January 15 (Monoghan 5.0 hrs; Hayden Ridge 0.7 hrs) 
 February 5 (SRC-Caw 2.3 hrs; Rocky Pass 2.0 hrs) 
 February 6 (Stearn 4.4 hrs; North Persimmon 1.8 hrs; North Berland 1.1 hrs) 
 February 9 (Swift-Horn 2.6 hrs; Triangle first half 2.5 hrs) 
 February 10 (Triangle second half 1.5 hrs; Moon and Planet 3.0 hrs; Mumm and Collie aborted 1.6 hrs) 
 February 14 (Sulphur 1.5 hrs; Ivy Ridge 1.7 hrs; Torrens aborted 0.5 hrs; plus 1.5 deadhead from Grande 
Prairie) 
 February 21 (Torrens 1.5; Horn-Gorman 1.4; Mt May 2.8; plus 1.8 deadhead from Grande Prairie) 
 February 26 (Brule-Solomon, Mumm and Collie, Stornoway JNP 5.2 hrs)
